extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in PTAB (part 42) proceedings; patent practitioners before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for requesting, processing, and deciding Director Review of Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions under 37 C.F.R. § 42.75, including who may request, eligible decisions, timing, content and formatting limits, standards of review, delegation, and post-decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Availability of Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request Director Review of: any decision on institution under 35 U.S.C. §§ 135, 314, or 324; any final decision under 35 U.S.C. §§ 135, 318, or 328; any decision granting rehearing of such decisions; or any other decision concluding a proceeding brought under 35 U.S.C. §§ 135, 311, or 321. The Director may also initiate Director Review sua sponte. 'Final decision' includes final written decisions in inter partes and post-grant review proceedings, as well as final decisions in derivations. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Arthrex addressed inter partes review, Director Review is available for other PTAB jurisdictions (post-grant review, derivation, etc.) for consistency and uniformity. Sua sponte review is expressly preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for Director Review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Director Review shall be limited to decisions presenting (a) an abuse of discretion, (b) important issues of law or policy, (c) erroneous findings of material fact, or (d) erroneous conclusions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both discretionary and merits-based issues may be raised, subject to the (a)–(d) limitations. For final decisions, all four grounds apply; for some institution-stage requests the same four grounds apply (text limits vary slightly by proceeding). Generally, a Director Review is not an opportunity to re-litigate institution-stage issues unless those issues fall within the permitted categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request Director Review / Amici participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a party to a proceeding before the Office may request Director Review. Third parties may not request Director Review or submit comments regarding a specific Director Review request or proceeding, aside from authorized amicus briefing. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For important issues of law or policy, the parties or third parties may request permission for amici to participate; the Director may also invite amici. Requests for amici participation should be concise (100 words or less) stating why participation may be appropriate and must not include merits argumentation. Any amicus brief by a party with whom the Director has a conflict will be stricken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-request limitation vs. rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is limited to requesting Director Review or rehearing by the Board, but shall not request both. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(c). An improper request for both Director Review and panel rehearing of the same decision will be treated as a request for Director Review only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must choose between the two remedies; filing both does not preserve both procedural tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing Director Review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review must be filed within the time period set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d) unless an extension is granted by the Director upon a showing of good cause. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely request for Director Review will be treated as a request for rehearing under 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(b)(1) and will reset the time for appeal until after all issues on Director Review are resolved. If a notice of appeal is filed before the request period expires, the Office will stay consideration of a subsequently filed request until the Federal Circuit determines whether to remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review shall be subject to the length limitations (i.e., 15 pages) for motions to the Board provided in 37 C.F.R. § 42.24(a)(1)(v), unless additional pages are authorized by the Director. The request must also conform to the applicable formatting requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a). 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses (if authorized) have their own page/time limits (see Response guidance). Requests must be filed in P-TACTS using the proper paper type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees due on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 42.15(f) is due on the filing of a request for Director Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure payment accompanies the filing per the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content restrictions — no new evidence or arguments without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent Director authorization, a request for Director Review may not introduce new evidence, and exhibits may not be entered in support of the request for Director Review. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(c)(3). The Director will not consider new evidence or new arguments not part of the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to authorization (which may be requested via email to Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov), new evidence or arguments may be allowed in cases of first impression or intervening changes in law or USPTO procedures. Any argument not made within the request may be deemed waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Director Review request — authorization and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A response to a request for Director Review is only permitted if authorized by the Director. For requests filed on or after February 3, 2025, the USPTO will send an email to parties authorizing a response. For requests filed on or after July 16, 2025, the response will be strictly limited to 15 pages and must be filed within five business days of the email. No new evidence may be filed with the response unless specifically authorized. The response must be filed in P-TACTS with the paper titled 'Authorized Response to Director Review Request'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the USPTO's email authorization and P-TACTS filing instructions exactly or the response may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and compliance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, the Office will catalog the request and review it to ensure compliance with requirements. If not compliant, the USPTO will attempt to work with the requesting party to rectify non-compliance. If non-compliance is due to untimeliness, the request will not be considered absent a good cause extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timeliness and compliance with page, formatting, fee, and content rules; the Office may assist with non-substantive compliance issues but not with untimely filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications must copy counsel and enter into record
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications from a party to the Office concerning a specific Director Review must copy (cc) counsel for all parties to the proceeding. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(g). All communications will be entered into the record of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to copy counsel may risk exclusion or record problems; communications become part of official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee consultation for important law/policy issues
rubrics_metrics.description: As to important issues of law or policy, the Director will consult an Advisory Committee to provide a recommendation. The Advisory Committee may provide a recommendation reflecting consensus or note differing views among its members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Committee includes representatives from five USPTO business units (Office of the Under Secretary; PTAB; Office of the Commissioner for Patents; Office of the General Counsel; Office of Policy and International Affairs) and may include technical experts or administrative support. The Committee's recommendation assists the Director but the Director retains final discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for non-policy issues
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests raising an abuse of discretion, erroneous findings of material fact, or erroneous conclusions of law but not raising important issues of law or policy, the Director will consult at least three members of the PTAB and may consult others as needed, provided no conflict of interest exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation is tailored to the nature of the issues raised; avoid conflicts when selecting consulted members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's decision-making and delegation options
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director receives each request, the underlying decision, associated arguments and evidence, and consulting recommendations, and determines whether to grant or deny Director Review or delegate further consideration to a Delegated Rehearing Panel (DRP). 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may issue an order granting review and identify issues or may grant and resolve issues in the first instance based on the existing record. The Director may also delegate review to the DRP when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegated Rehearing Panel (DRP) role and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate review of a Board decision to a Delegated Rehearing Panel. The DRP may be designated to consider whether a material issue of fact or law was misapprehended or overlooked. When delegated, the DRP panel will determine whether to grant rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation can occur from party requests or sua sponte; an order will identify delegation to the DRP. See Delegated Rehearing Panel web page for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review and possible dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Board under Director Review are reviewed de novo. Upon review, the Director may – in whole or in part – affirm, reverse, modify, vacate, or remand the decision to the Board for further proceedings. The Director may make any findings or conclusions deemed proper based on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De novo review permits full reconsideration of legal and factual determinations within the scope of the record and permitted issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to underlying proceeding and stays
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, the grant of Director Review does not stay the underlying proceeding before the Board; however, the Director maintains authority over all issues in the case during the pendency of Director Review, unless the Director orders otherwise. 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a stay is imposed, the Director will explicitly state it. The Director may delegate authority back to the Board for routine interlocutory matters outside the scope of Director Review while maintaining oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remands to the Board — timing and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Director remands a decision to the Board for further proceedings, absent a due date specified in the remand order or extension, the Board has established a goal to issue decisions in cases remanded from the Director as soon as possible and generally within six months of the date of remand even for complex records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure and pace of remand vary by case complexity, issues, Director instructions, and other circumstances. Upon remand, the Board issues an order setting a due date and must decide independently and without direction from the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions authority during Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has authority to impose sanctions against a party for misconduct committed during the course of Director Review (see 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(6); 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.11(d), 42.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions address abuse of discovery, abuse of process, harassment, unnecessary delay, misrepresentations, and other improper uses of the proceeding. The Board's sanction power is not limited to an enumerated list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Director Review decisions (routine, informative, precedential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Review decisions may be issued as precedential, informative, or routine decisions. Director Review decisions are, by default, routine decisions (SOP 2 and Addendum). Routine decisions may be nominated for precedential or informative designation following SOP 2 procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations are discretionary and the Director may designate or de-designate any decision or portion thereof at any time. The public may submit nominations (anonymously) via the PTAB Decision Nomination web form or email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of Director Review decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Director Review decision of a final decision under 35 U.S.C. §§ 135, 318, or 328, a decision granting rehearing of a final decision under those sections, or any other appealable decision concluding a proceeding under 35 U.S.C. §§ 135, 311, or 321 is appealable to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit using the same procedures for appealing other Board decisions. Director Review decisions of Board decisions on institution are not appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal treatment aligns with existing statutory appeal routes; institution decisions remain non-appealable under 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) and relevant precedent (e.g., Thryv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for rehearing of Director Review decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the time frame under 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d), a party may file one request for rehearing of a Director Review decision, but such requests should be rare and for very focused purposes. The rehearing request must specifically identify what matter the Director Review decision misapprehended or overlooked and is not an opportunity to raise new issues, reargue issues, or disagree generally with determinations by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party dissatisfied may file a single rehearing request without prior authorization; the party bears the burden of showing modification is warranted. Responses to rehearing are not permitted unless expressly authorized. A party must not file a request for rehearing of a Director's denial of Director Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and recusal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director, a consulting member of the PTAB, a member of the Advisory Committee, or other USPTO employee has a conflict of interest, they shall recuse themselves from the Director Review process for that decision. The USPTO follows the Standards of Ethical Conduct at 5 C.F.R. Part 2635 and consults the Department of Commerce Ethics Office as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts may include involvement in examination or prosecution of the underlying or related patents. PTAB members who consult or are Advisory Committee members follow SOP 1 and recuse themselves from discussion/analysis of cases on which they are paneled. The Office has procedures for potential conflicts by the Director (see Delegation of Authority / Director Recusal Procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sua sponte Director Review — purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate review sua sponte (on the Director’s own initiative). An order for sua sponte Director Review is treated like a timely request for rehearing for purposes of 37 C.F.R. § 90.3(b) and will reset the time for appeal to no later than 63 days after final resolution of the Director Review process. Absent exceptional circumstances, the Director may initiate sua sponte review at any point within 21 days after the expiration of the period for filing a request for rehearing, and before the filing of a notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sua sponte review is typically reserved for issues of exceptional importance. If initiated, the Director will issue an initial order notifying parties and the panel and may authorize briefing; the USPTO will set procedures if briefing is allowed.
